init.label: Choice Ladder
init.body:
# Choosing several options at once
A **Decision Matrix** ranks options. When you can pick several, but only within limits like a budget and a number of meals, the ranking alone isn't the answer: the top pick can eat so much of the budget that two good meals drop out.

The **Choice Ladder** walks the ranking one rung at a time toward the best plan. Each rung takes the best option that belongs in it and strikes off anything ranked above that doesn't fit or would crowd out more score than it brings. The bands down the sides are the dollars and meals: each card takes exactly what it spends.

A **toss-up** rung is where your weights, off by the **Wiggle**, can't tell two plans apart. Take the other option from the figure and the node keeps your pick; anything it displaced stays in the running if it still fits. Undo a pick on its card or on the node.

init.label: House projects
init.body:
### A second scenario
The same ladder on a year of house projects: $25,000 and ten free weekends. Disruption weighs against a project. The top-ranked Heat pump and the Roof patch are a toss-up at the first rung, and the ranking alone leaves money and weekends unused.
